newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Crude Outlook - technically-driven market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Crude Outlook - technically-driven market.

text.p: U.S. crude prices must prove the doubters wrong if gains are to made this week, as underlying technical pressures should work against attempts at price gains, traders and analysts said Monday.
The opposite was seen early Monday, with June crude futures on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) gaining around 20-25 cents to $19.80-85 a barrel.
However, crude prices remained in contango, with prices for nearby delivery at a discount to forward delivery, indicating negative sentiment in the market, traders said.
Traders said June crude futures must settle above the 20-day moving average at $19.78 a barrel to abate near-term bearishness.

"There was (technical) damage done on Friday," noted William Brown, president of W.H. Brown & Co in New York. He said a scenario in which prompt June prices retest the $19.00 a barrel mark was likely, an assertion backed-up by his prediction for negative results for weekly inventory data.
"I see the inventory stats being less than constructive, and after our inability to break through $20.50, it looks like we could be in a $1.50 trading range," Brown said.
Expectations for bearish American Petroleum Institute (API) and Department of Energy (DOE) reports are based on calls for lower gasoline demand numbers.
"After two weeks of gasoline demand levels at inordinately high levels, I think we are due for lower demand. Numbers have been especially volatile in the API's," said Brown.
Further, Brown said weakness in gasoline should result in an extremely short "gasoline season" this year, from later this week through Memorial Day.
"Markets are more and more willing to discount seasonal trends earlier and earlier," said Brown.

Tom Bentz, director of energy trading for High Yield Analytics in New York, said he also foresees a technical test of lower numbers, noting the recent low marks for June futures aat $18.96 and $19.00 were keys for immediate direction.
"The spreads are still in contango, and there is still a negative feeling hanging in the market," Bentz said.
However, unlike many bears in the cash markets, Bentz said he thinks the markets are fundamentally balanced.

Cash dealers said domestic grade barrels could be mixed this week. West Texas Intermediate/Cushing to Brent spreads have fluctuated in recent days, with most feeling the arbitrage spread has now narrowed, eliminating some pressure on grades.

"We could see steady numbers, but it's hard to tell with so many players out of the market last Thursday and Friday. Monday has started slowly, but it should pick-up when the refiners come looking for barrels," said a Texas cash trader.

Key sweet grades, like Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James were around flat to 5 cents under outright June benchmark WTI/Cushing. These levels are nearly identical to numbers that were pegged last Monday, as are differentials for Midland/WTI, Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire and the sour grades.
